title: The derived exchange transformation commutes with shifts and maps triangles to morphisms of triangles
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$, and let $\Ex_\square:\Phi:=g^{-1}Rf_*\to\Psi:=Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ be the derived exchange transformation of functors $\Dplus(X_{\Et})\to\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Write $[1]$ for the shift of complexes, $(M[1])^r=M^{r+1}$, $d_{M[1]}=-d_M$. Give each of the four functors $u^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and $Ru_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] its shift-commutation isomorphism: for $u^{-1}$ the identity $u^{-1}(M[1])=(u^{-1}M)[1]$ of termwise shifted complexes; for $Ru_*$ the isomorphism $Ru_*(K[1])\cong u_*(I(K)[1])=(u_*I(K))[1]$ obtained by comparing the K-injective resolution $K[1]\to I(K[1])$ with the K-injective resolution $K[1]\to I(K)[1]$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. Let $\xi_K:\Phi(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi(K)[1]$ and $\zeta_K:\Psi(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Psi(K)[1]$ be the composite shift-commutation isomorphisms, and $\xi^{(n)}_K:\Phi(K[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi(K)[n]$, $\zeta^{(n)}_K$ ($n\in\mathbf Z$) their iterates (for $n<0$ the inverses of the iterates at $K[n]$). Then:

(1) for every $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$, $\zeta_K\circ\Ex_{\square,K[1]}=\Ex_{\square,K}[1]\circ\xi_K$; hence $\zeta^{(n)}_K\circ\Ex_{\square,K[n]}=\Ex_{\square,K}[n]\circ\xi^{(n)}_K$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$;

(2) for every triangle $X_1\xrightarrow{u}X_2\xrightarrow{v}X_3\xrightarrow{w}X_1[1]$ in $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift], the triple $(\Ex_{\square,X_1},\Ex_{\square,X_2},\Ex_{\square,X_3})$ is a morphism of triangles from $(\Phi X_1,\Phi X_2,\Phi X_3,\Phi u,\Phi v,\xi_{X_1}\circ\Phi w)$ to $(\Psi X_1,\Psi X_2,\Psi X_3,\Psi u,\Psi v,\zeta_{X_1}\circ\Psi w)$.

(Part (2) follows from (1) and the naturality of $\Ex_\square$; part (1) says that $\Ex_\square$ is a morphism of triangulated functors.)

source.place: Lemma 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact, line 2290): the right adjoint of an exact functor is exact, with the shift isomorphism G(A)[1] -> G(A[1]) adjoint to eps_A[1] o xi_{G(A)}; applied to the adjunctions f^{-1} -| Rf_*, f'^{-1} -| Rf'_* and to the base change map of literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex, equation (equation-base-change), line 18332, defined in literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex, Remark (remark-base-change), line 4033, as a composite of unit, square isomorphism and counit. The statement is assembled by an agent: the Stacks project uses it without stating it (Lemma 0DDE, 'some details omitted').

proof.text: **Step 1 (the shift isomorphisms of all functors involved).** Every inverse image $u^{-1}$ ($u\in\{f,g,f',g'\}$) carries $\iota^u_M:u^{-1}(M[1])=(u^{-1}M)[1]$, the identity of the termwise shifted complex [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]; every $Ru_*$ ($u\in\{f,f'\}$) carries $\sigma^u_K:Ru_*(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(Ru_*K)[1]$, the comparison of K-injective resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]; a composite functor carries the composite isomorphism $\chi_X=\gamma_{FX}\circ G(\varphi_X)$ [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite], which does not depend on how a composite of three or more functors is bracketed ([lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] (iv)). In particular $\xi_K=\iota^g_{Rf_*K}\circ g^{-1}(\sigma^f_K)$ and $\zeta_K=\sigma^{f'}_{g'^{-1}K}\circ Rf'_*(\iota^{g'}_K)$ are the isomorphisms $\xi,\zeta$ of the statement, and the intermediate functors $\Phi_1=Rf'_*f'^{-1}g^{-1}Rf_*$ and $\Phi_2=Rf'_*g'^{-1}f^{-1}Rf_*$ carry composite isomorphisms $\chi^1,\chi^2$.

proof.text: **Step 2 (Ex as a composite of three whiskered transformations).** By [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], $\Ex_{\square,K}=c_K\circ b_K\circ a_K$ with $a=\eta^D_{f'}\Phi:\Phi\to\Phi_1$, $a_K=\eta^D_{f',\Phi K}$ (the unit of $f'^{-1}\dashv Rf'_*$ precomposed with $\Phi=g^{-1}Rf_*$); $b=Rf'_*\theta^D_\square Rf_*:\Phi_1\to\Phi_2$, $b_K=Rf'_*(\theta^D_{\square,Rf_*K})$; $c=Rf'_*g'^{-1}\varepsilon^D_f:\Phi_2\to\Psi$, $c_K=Rf'_*g'^{-1}(\varepsilon^D_{f,K})$. This is the explicit formula of the definition, read as an identity of natural transformations.

source.place: Lemma 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact, line 2290) and Definition 014V (line 191); the base change map as unit, square isomorphism and counit: literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex, Remark remark-base-change (line 4033)

proof.text: **Step 3 (each ingredient commutes with the shift).** (a) By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-commshift] (b) for $u=f'$, the unit $\eta^D_{f'}:\mathrm{id}\to Rf'_*f'^{-1}$ is compatible with the shift: $\sigma^{f'}_{f'^{-1}M}\circ Rf'_*(\iota^{f'}_M)\circ\eta^D_{f',M[1]}=\eta^D_{f',M}[1]$, the left-hand isomorphism being the composite isomorphism of $Rf'_*f'^{-1}$ and the identity functor carrying the identity. (b) By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-commshift] (a) for $u=f$, the counit $\varepsilon^D_f:f^{-1}Rf_*\to\mathrm{id}$ is compatible with the shift: $\varepsilon^D_{f,K[1]}=\varepsilon^D_{f,K}[1]\circ\iota^f_{Rf_*K}\circ f^{-1}(\sigma^f_K)$. (c) By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso-commshift], $\theta^D_\square:f'^{-1}g^{-1}\to g'^{-1}f^{-1}$ is compatible with the composite shift isomorphisms $\varphi,\psi$ of the two composites of inverse images.

source.place: Lemma 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact, line 2290) and Definition 014V (line 191); the base change map as unit, square isomorphism and counit: literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex, Remark remark-base-change (line 4033)

proof.text: **Step 4 (part (1) for $n=1$).** By [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] (iii) with $F=\Phi$, $a=\eta^D_{f'}\Phi$ is compatible with the shift: $\chi^1_K\circ a_{K[1]}=a_K[1]\circ\xi_K$. (Directly: $\chi^1_K=\sigma^{f'}_{f'^{-1}\Phi K}\circ Rf'_*(\iota^{f'}_{\Phi K})\circ Rf'_*f'^{-1}(\xi_K)$, and naturality of $\eta^D_{f'}$ for $\xi_K$ followed by Step 3(a) at $M=\Phi K$ gives $\chi^1_K\circ\eta^D_{f',\Phi(K[1])}=\eta^D_{f',\Phi K}[1]\circ\xi_K$.) By (iii) with $F=Rf_*$ and then (ii) with $G=Rf'_*$, $b$ is compatible: $\chi^2_K\circ b_{K[1]}=b_K[1]\circ\chi^1_K$. By (ii) with $G=Rf'_*g'^{-1}$, $c$ is compatible: $\zeta_K\circ c_{K[1]}=c_K[1]\circ\chi^2_K$ (the identity functor carrying the identity isomorphism, the composite isomorphism of $Rf'_*g'^{-1}\circ\mathrm{id}$ is $\zeta$). Composing, by (i): $\zeta_K\circ\Ex_{\square,K[1]}=\zeta_K\circ c_{K[1]}\circ b_{K[1]}\circ a_{K[1]}=c_K[1]\circ\chi^2_K\circ b_{K[1]}\circ a_{K[1]}=c_K[1]\circ b_K[1]\circ\chi^1_K\circ a_{K[1]}=c_K[1]\circ b_K[1]\circ a_K[1]\circ\xi_K=\Ex_{\square,K}[1]\circ\xi_K$, using that $[1]$ is a functor. This is (1) for $n=1$: $\Ex_\square$ is a morphism of triangulated functors.

source.place: Lemma 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact, line 2290) and Definition 014V (line 191); the base change map as unit, square isomorphism and counit: literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex, Remark remark-base-change (line 4033)

proof.text: **Step 5 (part (1) for all $n$).** For $n=0$, $\xi^{(0)}=\zeta^{(0)}=\mathrm{id}$. For $n\ge1$, $\xi^{(n+1)}_K=\xi^{(n)}_K[1]\circ\xi_{K[n]}$ and likewise for $\zeta$, so by induction, Step 4 at $K[n]$ and functoriality of $[1]$: $\zeta^{(n+1)}_K\circ\Ex_{K[n+1]}=\zeta^{(n)}_K[1]\circ\zeta_{K[n]}\circ\Ex_{K[n][1]}=\zeta^{(n)}_K[1]\circ\Ex_{K[n]}[1]\circ\xi_{K[n]}=(\Ex_K[n]\circ\xi^{(n)}_K)[1]\circ\xi_{K[n]}=\Ex_K[n+1]\circ\xi^{(n+1)}_K$. For $n=-m<0$, $\xi^{(-m)}_K=\bigl((\xi^{(m)}_{K[-m]})^{-1}\bigr)[-m]$ and likewise for $\zeta$ (the shift of complexes satisfies $[m][-m]=\mathrm{id}$); the case $m$ at $K[-m]$, $\zeta^{(m)}_{K[-m]}\circ\Ex_K=\Ex_{K[-m]}[m]\circ\xi^{(m)}_{K[-m]}$, rearranges to $(\zeta^{(m)}_{K[-m]})^{-1}\circ\Ex_{K[-m]}[m]=\Ex_K\circ(\xi^{(m)}_{K[-m]})^{-1}$, and applying $[-m]$ gives $\zeta^{(-m)}_K\circ\Ex_{K[-m]}=\Ex_K[-m]\circ\xi^{(-m)}_K$.

source.place: Lemma 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact, line 2290) and Definition 014V (line 191); the base change map as unit, square isomorphism and counit: literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex, Remark remark-base-change (line 4033)

proof.text: **Step 6 (part (2)).** Apply [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-triangle-morphism] to $F_1=\Phi$ with $\varphi=\xi$, $F_2=\Psi$ with $\psi=\zeta$ and $\tau=\Ex_\square$, which is natural [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] and compatible with the shift by Step 4. Explicitly, for a triangle $X_1\xrightarrow{u}X_2\xrightarrow{v}X_3\xrightarrow{w}X_1[1]$: $\Psi u\circ\Ex_{X_1}=\Ex_{X_2}\circ\Phi u$ and $\Psi v\circ\Ex_{X_2}=\Ex_{X_3}\circ\Phi v$ by naturality, and $\zeta_{X_1}\circ\Psi w\circ\Ex_{X_3}=\zeta_{X_1}\circ\Ex_{X_1[1]}\circ\Phi w=\Ex_{X_1}[1]\circ\xi_{X_1}\circ\Phi w$ by naturality for $w$ and Step 4 at $X_1$; these are the three squares of a morphism of triangles [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift].
